title: Pointwise colimits extend a lift across its relative mapping cylinder
statement:
Use coherent functors, quasicategories, simplicial pullbacks and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and relative joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. All the following objects fit in one fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $K,X,Y$ be quasicategories, let $a:K\to X$ be a functor and $q:Y\to X$ a cocartesian fibration. For an edge $e:z\to z'$, a transport functor means a functor $e_!:Y_z\to Y_{z'}$ equipped with a simplicial map $H:Y_z\times\Delta^1\to Y$ over $e\circ\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^1}$ whose initial endpoint is the fiber inclusion, whose final endpoint is the fiber inclusion composed with $e_!$, and whose edge on each $\{v\}\times\Delta^1$ is $q$-cocartesian. Put $T_a=K\star_X X$, where the second map to $X$ is its identity, and let $\pi:T_a\to X$ be its structural map. Thus a map $U\to T_a$ consists of a map $\epsilon:U\to\Delta^1$, a map $\xi:U\times_{\Delta^1}\{0\}\to K$, and a map $\chi:U\to X$ satisfying $\chi|_{U\times_{\Delta^1}\{0\}}=a\xi$; in particular $T_a$ contains its canonical copies of $K$ and $X$.

For $x\in X$, let $X_{/x}$ be the slice of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]: its $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to X$ ending at $x$, with source projection the entire initial face. Put $L_x=K\times_X X_{/x}$. Suppose that, for every pair of vertices $x,z\in X$, the fiber $Y_z$ admits colimits of every diagram indexed by $L_x$, and that every edge transport $Y_z\to Y_{z'}$ preserves these $L_x$-indexed colimits. Then every functor $f:K\to Y$ with $qf=a$ has a simplicial extension $F:T_a\to Y$ satisfying $F|_K=f$ and $qF=\pi$ exactly. There is no filteredness hypothesis on $Y_z$ and no size bound on the fibers beyond the containing universe. Empty shapes $L_x$ require initial objects and their preservation.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.2.13 (existence along a full inclusion) and Corollary 4.3.1.11 (relative colimits from fiber colimits and preservation); the construction T(K) and its slice K ×_X X_{/x} in the proof of Lemma 5.4.4.2, printed pp. 432-433. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: First verify the source geometry rather than assuming that an arbitrary relative join is a quasicategory. Reversing the two ordered vertex blocks in [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] identifies $(T_a)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $X^{\mathrm{op}}\star_{X^{\mathrm{op}}}K^{\mathrm{op}}$, formed with $\mathrm{id}$ and $a^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-join-cartesian-realization] to $a^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the opposite-quasicategory clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. Thus $T_a$ is a quasicategory and its $K$-copy is full. Put $J_c=K\times_{T_a}(T_a)_{/c}$ and let $r_c:J_c\to K$ be its source projection and $k_c:J_c^{\triangleright}\to T_a$ its canonical cocone. If $c=i_X(x)$, the simplex formula identifies $J_c$ exactly with $L_x$: an $n$-simplex has its first $n+1$ vertices in the $K$ block and last vertex $x$, so its data are $\tau\in K_n$ and $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to X$ with $\sigma|_{[n]}=a\tau$ and $\sigma(n+1)=x$. Operators restrict the first $n+1$ vertices and retain the last. Under this identification $r_c$ is the projection of $L_x$, and $\pi k_c$ is the canonical slice cocone in $X$. If $c=i_K(k)$, all vertices are in the full $K$-copy, so $J_c=K_{/k}$ and $k_c$ is its canonical cocone followed by $i_K$. These identifications commute with every simplicial operator, including degeneracies.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.4.2, relative cylinder T(K) and the slices at its vertices; Kerodon 024K supplies the opposite relative-join realization.

proof.text: The map $q$ is an isofibration. It is an inner fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Given an equivalence $\alpha:q(y)\to x$, choose a $q$-cocartesian lift $e:y\to y\prime$ with the prescribed source. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], for every $z$ its precomposition square on mapping spaces is a homotopy pullback. The bottom horizontal map is an equivalence, since precomposition with an inverse of $\alpha$ is its homotopy inverse. Consequently the top horizontal map $e^*:\operatorname{Map}_Y(y\prime,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(y,z)$ is an equivalence: in the path-pullback model the projection along a homotopy equivalence has contractible fibers. On connected components take $z=y$ to obtain $r:y\prime\to y$ with $re=1_y$. Taking $z=y\prime$, injectivity of $e^*$ and $(er)e=e=1_{y\prime}e$ give $er=1_{y\prime}$ in the homotopy category. Thus $e$ is an equivalence and lifts $\alpha$ exactly, as required.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.3.2.13, categorical-fibration hypothesis; dual mapping-space criterion for cocartesian edges.

proof.text: At a $K$-vertex $k$, the indexing quasicategory is $J_{i_K(k)}=K_{/k}$ by Step 1 and [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Its vertex $t=1_k$ is final by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final]. Every fiber $Y_z$ is a quasicategory: an inner-horn problem there is a problem for $q$ over the constant simplex at $z$, so the inner-fibration filler stays in that fiber by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. For any diagram $d:K_{/k}\to Y_z$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] to obtain a coherent cocone with vertex $d(t)$ whose leg at $t$ is the identity of $d(t)$. That node phrases colimits by mapping spaces; to obtain a colimiting cocone in the initial-object sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] used in Step 5, note that the degenerate identity edge is an equivalence edge (it is its own inverse, with degenerate $2$-simplices as witnesses), so [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-cocone-criterion] shows that this cocone is colimiting. Thus every fiber has colimits of this shape.

source.place: HTT Remark 4.3.2.3 (vertices already in the full subcategory); final-object colimit calculation.

proof.text: For any colimiting cocone $\lambda:d\to\Delta l$ in $Y_z$, [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-cocone-criterion] says that $\lambda_t:d(t)\to l$ is an equivalence. Let $e_!:Y_z\to Y_{z\prime}$ be any edge transport. As a simplicial map, $e_!$ takes an inverse edge and both inverse-triangle $2$-simplices of $\lambda_t$ to the same inverse data for $e_!(\lambda_t)$. The leg of the image cocone $e_!\lambda$ at $t$ is exactly $e_!(\lambda_t)$, so it is an equivalence. Apply the same cited criterion in $Y_{z\prime}$ to conclude that $e_!\lambda$ is colimiting. Consequently every edge transport preserves all $K_{/k}$-indexed colimits. This supplies the preservation hypothesis at $K$-vertices without adding an assumption.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.5, absolute final-index cocone criterion; apply the equivalence-edge definition to the transport simplicial map.

proof.text: For each vertex $c$ of $T_a$, apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-prescribed-cone-colimit-lifting] with $p=q$, $J=J_c$, $h=fr_c$ and $g=\pi k_c$. The compatibility is exact: $qfr_c=ar_c=(\pi k_c)|_{J_c}$. For $c=i_X(x)$ the required fiber colimits and preservation are precisely the hypotheses for $L_x$ in the statement, using the exact slice identification in Step 1. For $c=i_K(k)$ they were verified in Steps 3 and 4. All these simplicial sets are small in the common containing universe. The cited lemma gives a $q$-colimit diagram $v_c:J_c^{\triangleright}\to Y$ with $v_c|_{J_c}=fr_c$ and $qv_c=\pi k_c$ exactly. In particular these cones lie over the varying canonical base cones; a cone entirely inside $Y_x$ would not by itself have that property. For an empty $L_x$ the same lemma uses the assumed preserved initial objects.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.3.1.11 applied to each local cone in Lemma 4.3.2.13.

proof.text: Now apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence] with $\mathcal A=K$, $\mathcal C=T_a$, $\mathcal D=Y$, $\mathcal B=X$, $p=q$, $h=f$ and $s=\pi$. Step 1 gives a full subcategory of a quasicategory; Step 2 verifies the isofibration; the equation $qf=a=\pi|_K$ is the given equality; and Step 5 supplies every local $q$-colimit lift with the required exact boundary and base. The conclusion is a simplicial map $F:T_a\to Y$ with $F|_K=f$ and $qF=\pi$ exactly. No filteredness, extra colimits, or size condition outside the containing universe was used.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.3.2.13, applied as in the final paragraph of Lemma 5.4.4.2.

proof_origin.place: Historical blueprint ancestor, proof paragraph 2: coherent finite-coefficient adjunction infrastructure. The one-level proof follows the online HTT 5.4.4.2 route through 4.3.1.11 and 4.3.2.13; these texts are not archived.
